entities.summary:
Nominoe (d. March 11, 851), often revered as the "Father of the Country" (Tad ar Vro) by Breton nationalists, was the first Duke of Brittany, reigning from 846 until his death. His career, unfolding amidst the tumultuous fragmentation of the Carolingian Empire, fundamentally shaped the political landscape of western Francia and established the enduring autonomy of Brittany. Initially a trusted administrator appointed by Emperor Louis the Pious in 831 as *missus imperatoris* (imperial envoy) for Brittany, Nominoe skillfully leveraged the internal strife of the Frankish realm to transform a regional governorship into a de facto independent state.

His ascension to power began with imperial sanction, yet Nominoe quickly capitalized on the weakening central authority of the Carolingian emperors. Following Louis the Pious's death in 840, Nominoe found himself increasingly at odds with Charles the Bald, ruler of West Francia. This conflict culminated in the decisive Battle of Ballon on November 22, 845, where Nominoe's Breton forces inflicted a significant defeat upon Charles the Bald's army. This victory secured Breton independence, compelling Charles to recognize Nominoe as Duke of Brittany in 846, albeit under nominal Frankish suzerainty. Nominoe then expanded Breton influence, campaigning aggressively into the March of Brittany and conquering territories including Rennes and Nantes, effectively establishing the territorial boundaries of the future Duchy.
